therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: in vivo detection and quantification of cerebral amyloid deposition
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus undergoing brain biopsy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: correlation between quantitative brain uptake (SUVR) of [18F]flutemetamol and immunohistochemical estimates of amyloid levels in biopsy samples

results.effect_size: R² = 0.688 (composite SUVR vs IHC amyloid), p = 0.098
results.target_engagement_evidence: SUVR values ranged from 1.00 to 2.86 across brain regions and subjects; IHC percent plaque area ranged from 0 to 1.007%
biomarker_changes: Composite VOI SUVR ranged from 1.34 to 2.74 across 7 subjects
IHC percent plaque area (NAB228): subjects 201-0003, 201-0006, 201-0007 had 0% plaque; subject 201-0004 had highest plaque load at 1.007%
Linear regression of composite SUVR vs IHC amyloid: R² = 0.688, p = 0.098
subgroup_findings: Subject 201-0004 had highest SUVR values across all brain regions (composite 2.74) and highest IHC plaque load (1.007%)
Subject 201-0007 had lowest SUVR values (composite 1.34) and zero IHC plaque load
Subjects 201-0003, 201-0006, 201-0007 had zero IHC plaque load with lower SUVR values
Anterior cingulate and posterior cortex showed highest SUVR values across subjects

context.comparator: immunohistochemical biopsy analysis (ex vivo reference standard)
context.duration: single imaging session; trial ran December 2009 to August 2010
context.investigator_commentary: This was a small feasibility study (n=7) correlating in vivo PET amyloid imaging with ex vivo biopsy IHC. The linear regression between composite SUVR and IHC amyloid approached but did not reach statistical significance (R²=0.688, p=0.098), likely due to the very small sample size.
